UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE and TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS exist in the schema taxonomy and are written by nothing

provenThreeWays: SOURCE: the single orchestrator call site passes a hardcoded attemptNo: 1 (rootRunner.ts:374); no retry, backoff or re-attempt loop exists anywhere under src/orgunits/web/ or src/orgunits/orchestrator/

TESTS: phase2b.firewall.test.ts asserts the gateway source matches no /\b(retry|retries|backoff|pRetry)\b/i, and orgunitGateway.test.ts 'does not retry a timeout, a 429 or a 500' asserts exactly one transport plan for each of READ_TIMEOUT, CONNECT_TIMEOUT, a 429 carrying Retry-After, and a 500
DURABLE EVIDENCE: a join of every error-bearing observation to any same-(run, root, url) row with a higher attempt_no returns 0
retryCountToday.attemptNoTwoRowsAreNotRetries: both are HTTP 200 robots-path reads inside the two Option-C-lite v3 runs, produced by RobotsCache.nextPolicyAttemptNo; two attempts at one URL made for two different reasons, never a repetition of a failure

circuitBreakerAndRobotsBootstrap.question: does the root terminate before a 3-failure transient threshold could matter?
circuitBreakerAndRobotsBootstrap.answer: YES, and the finding is stronger than the question
circuitBreakerAndRobotsBootstrap.strongerFinding: a policy-bootstrap failure exits attemptUrl on the BLOCKED path at rootRunner.ts:421-428, which returns BEFORE updateCircuitBreaker is reached at rootRunner.ts:433. The breaker is never told about the failure at all; its state for that host stays CLOSED / streak 0 for the whole run.
circuitBreakerAndRobotsBootstrap.supportingEvidence: index 8's record reports circuitOpenHosts = 0 on a run whose only request failed at TLS
circuitBreakerAndRobotsBootstrap.failedPolicyIsMemoisedForTheRun: cache.set(runId, scheme, hostname, pending) at robots.ts:541 is unconditional, so a FETCH_FAILED policy is cached with the same permanence as a parsed one

tlsHeterogeneityFinding.additionalAsymmetry: the one genuinely retryable TLS condition is already split across CONNECT_TIMEOUT and TLS_FAILURE depending on which of two timers fires first

localArtifactSearch.consistentWithTheCodeFinding: errorDetail never reached stdout, so no terminal capture could have contained it

cases.case: lookup succeeded but returned no address of either family
cases.nodeCode: none - a separate code path in the gateway

dnsAudit.statedClearly: NO. A safe retry policy cannot distinguish a transient DNS failure from a permanent one using today's durable evidence.
dnsAudit.whyPermanent: the row is append-only and nwf_research holds no UPDATE grant, so a future subtype column can never be back-filled onto it

reasoning.502_503_504: RFC 9110 defines all three as intermediary or capacity conditions - bad upstream response, temporary overload or maintenance, upstream timeout - so all three are semantically transient; 503 is additionally the status for which Retry-After is specifically defined
reasoning.500: a generic unqualified server error carrying no claim about duration; index 3 returning 500 on two different paths is at least as consistent with a site-wide deterministic fault as with a transient one

http5xxAudit.retryAfterAppearsInTheRepositoryOnlyAs: an input in a test fixture asserting that a 429 carrying it is NOT retried
http5xxAudit.honouringRetryAfterWouldRequire: reading a fifth response header and letting a third party influence this process's timing - a real widening of the request boundary

robotsBootstrapSinglePointOfFailure.precisely: one transport failure on the robots bootstrap currently makes that host/root a single-attempt single point of failure; the entire origin becomes unfetchable for the run after exactly one request

contrastWithOrdinaryPageDiscovery.ordinaryPageFailureScope: one URL out of up to 35 page attempts, 3000 sitemap URLs and 8 hosts
contrastWithOrdinaryPageDiscovery.durableControlCase: index 5's SUCCESSFUL v2 run contains a READ_TIMEOUT on a LINK request and still produced 33 raw pages

robotsBootstrapSinglePointOfFailure.wasThisAnExplicitDesignChoice: PARTLY - the two halves must be separated

explicitlyChosen.verdict: deliberate, reasoned, and NOT questioned by this audit

notChosen.what: that the policy is attempted exactly once
notChosen.why: a consequence of (a) RobotsCache memoising the in-flight promise, whose ADR 0006 rationale is given entirely in terms of politeness and concurrency de-duplication and which nowhere discusses what memoising a FAILED policy fetch implies, and (b) the absence of any retry policy above the gateway
notChosen.consequenceForDesign: a bounded bootstrap retry would NOT weaken ADR 0006's fail-closed posture - an unread policy would still block every page - it would revisit a caching decision made for concurrency reasons with an unexamined resilience side effect

properties.attemptNoPlusOne: supported and already exercised in production (two attempt_no = 2 rows exist)
properties.separatelyPersisted: supported - attempt_no is part of the unique identity
properties.independentlyDnsResolved: supported - the pinned-lookup guard throws if resolution is attempted more than once within one attempt
properties.independentlyIpSsrfValidated: supported - every returned address re-classified, any forbidden one refuses the whole host
properties.separatelyChargedToRequestBudget: supported mechanically, with one caveat: predictedCost is a prediction and RequestBudget.consume THROWS rather than clamping, so a retrying caller must predict its own extra request
properties.subjectToPacing: supported if routed through attemptUrl; a retry issued on any other path would bypass pacer.waitForSlot
properties.noAlternateHostname: supported - scope is re-derived from the root authority, never from the caller
properties.noAlternateProtocol: supported - HTTPS to HTTP downgrade refused
properties.noWeakerTls: supported - no TLS option is caller-controllable
properties.noDifferentUserAgent: supported - REQUEST_HEADERS is a frozen module constant
properties.noProxy: supported - node:http/node:https read no proxy variables
properties.noCookiesOrSession: supported - set-cookie is dropped, not joined; no jar exists

whatIsMissing: a caller that decides to retry

for a BOOTSTRAP retry specifically: RobotsCache memoises a FETCH_FAILED policy unconditionally, so a second bootstrap attempt would read the cached failure rather than making a request; a design must choose deliberate non-memoisation or explicit invalidation, and restate ADR 0006's request-count invariants
for a BOOTSTRAP retry specifically: the circuit breaker is never informed of a bootstrap failure, so a retried bootstrap would consume attempts without the breaker counting them

A_KEEP_CURRENT_ONE_SHOT_POLICY.methodologicalCleanliness: HIGHEST - one request, one row, one outcome
A_KEEP_CURRENT_ONE_SHOT_POLICY.networkSafety: HIGHEST - strictly fewer third-party requests than any alternative
A_KEEP_CURRENT_ONE_SHOT_POLICY.reservePressure: HIGHEST - every transient blip is paid for with a non-renewable reserve slot
A_KEEP_CURRENT_ONE_SHOT_POLICY.vulnerabilityToTransientNoise: HIGHEST and structurally asymmetric - a single packet-timing accident on the robots bootstrap costs an entire organisation while the same accident on an ordinary page costs one frontier entry
A_KEEP_CURRENT_ONE_SHOT_POLICY.honestSummary: the cleanest and safest option, which buys those properties by letting acquisition outcomes depend on single-sample network luck at exactly the point where a single sample is most expensive

B_BOUNDED_RETRY_FOR_UNAMBIGUOUS_TRANSIEN.whyExcluded: neither can be safely subdivided with today's durable evidence
B_BOUNDED_RETRY_FOR_UNAMBIGUOUS_TRANSIEN.connectionRefusedCaveat: ECONNREFUSED means a reachable host actively answered with a RST - a deterministic answer, not a timing accident - so it is the weakest member of the set and could defensibly be dropped
B_BOUNDED_RETRY_FOR_UNAMBIGUOUS_TRANSIEN.definableFromDurableEvidence: COMPLETE - all four categories are the persisted error_kind itself
B_BOUNDED_RETRY_FOR_UNAMBIGUOUS_TRANSIEN.methodologicalCleanliness: GOOD - preregisterable, category-based, mechanically checkable; costs one clear statement that an acquisition failure means two failed attempts rather than one
B_BOUNDED_RETRY_FOR_UNAMBIGUOUS_TRANSIEN.networkSafety: adds at most one request per failing URL, inside the frozen 60-request ceiling, under existing pacing
B_BOUNDED_RETRY_FOR_UNAMBIGUOUS_TRANSIEN.summary: correct, cheap, and on everything measured so far inert

C_SPLIT_TRANSPORT_FAILURE_TAXONOMY_FIRST.migrationCost: one additive nullable column plus one CHECK; no table rewrite, no grant change, no data movement
C_SPLIT_TRANSPORT_FAILURE_TAXONOMY_FIRST.provenanceCost: REAL AND PERMANENT - append-only plus no UPDATE grant means every existing row stays NULL forever; the taxonomy is strictly prospective
C_SPLIT_TRANSPORT_FAILURE_TAXONOMY_FIRST.doesItHelpIndices3_4_6_8: NO - not now and not ever
C_SPLIT_TRANSPORT_FAILURE_TAXONOMY_FIRST.whatItUnlocks: the only two classes that cover anything actually observed

D1_502_503_504_only.semanticFooting: STRONG - RFC 9110 defines all three as intermediary or capacity conditions

D2_blanket_500_as_well.methodologicalCaution: risks re-requesting a deterministic application fault

D_BOUNDED_HTTP_SERVICE_RETRY.safety: a 5xx means the host is alive and answering; a second request is cheap for the site relative to a timeout
D_BOUNDED_HTTP_SERVICE_RETRY.retryAfterShapeWorthConsidering: honour it only as a LOWER bound on the existing pacing delay, up to a frozen ceiling; never let it shorten a wait, never let it exceed the run's own budget

E_COMBINED_OBSERVABILITY_PLUS_NARROW_RET.composition: Option C's taxonomy, plus one exact-request retry for B's four error_kind classes, C's TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT and DNS_TEMPORARY_FAILURE subtypes, and D1's 502/503/504
E_COMBINED_OBSERVABILITY_PLUS_NARROW_RET.whyCoherent: the evidence records the CONDITION and the policy DERIVES retryability from it, so a future change to what counts as retryable does not require new acquisition - the same separation website_claims enforces between an immutable claim and a derived verdict, applied to transport evidence
E_COMBINED_OBSERVABILITY_PLUS_NARROW_RET.cost: the largest change - migration, ADR, policy bump, plan amendment - and its retry half cannot be correctly scoped until its observability half has run long enough to show what the subtypes actually contain

proposedMinimalDurableSubtypeSchema.constrainedBy: one CHECK over a closed 8-member vocabulary, in the same shape as the landed error_kind CHECK
proposedMinimalDurableSubtypeSchema.populatedBy: a pure deterministic mapping function from the Node condition
proposedMinimalDurableSubtypeSchema.whyNotStored: storing a retry verdict in evidence would repeat the website_claims mistake of freezing a conclusion into an immutable claim

nodeConditions: any other ERR_TLS_ or ERR_SSL_ prefix

nullSemanticsObligation.whyFetchPolicyVersionIsNotTheDiscriminat: coupling an observability column to a request-boundary version would be a category error

deliberatelyDeferredExpansion.whyDeferred: not required by any retry decision, since all three are equally non-retryable; left out of the minimal proposal on purpose rather than by omission

futureRetryDecisionsItUnlocks: whether a DNS_FAILURE may be retried at all - answerable only once DNS_TEMPORARY_FAILURE is separable from DNS_NAME_NOT_FOUND

whether a TLS_FAILURE may be retried at all - answerable only once TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT is separable from TLS_CERT_INVALID; today retrying the class would mean re-requesting expired-certificate hosts five times out of six

whether the robots-bootstrap single point of failure is worth repairing - answerable only once it is known what share of bootstrap failures are timing-dependent rather than deterministic, which is currently UNKNOWN in both directions

ruleDefinitionDiscipline.clearestEvidenceTheConstraintHeld: the recommended direction classifies three of the four current failures as unclassifiable and helps none of them, which is not an outcome a rule reverse-engineered from those four cases would produce

counterfactualEligibility.failure: HTTP 500 on root and conventional sitemap

counterfactualReading: Option B is inert on everything observed
Option C converts three NOT_RETRY_ELIGIBLE into three honest INSUFFICIENT_PERSISTED_DETAIL_TO_CLASSIFY - a gain in truthfulness, not in recovery, and only for future rows
only D2 produces a single eligible case, on the sub-rule with the weakest semantic footing

reasonsIndependentOfAnyExtrapolation: the reserve is finite, non-renewable and shared across the whole generation; the four failures already on the books would consume 4 of the 40 - a tenth of the entire buffer - against 9 of 110 primary slots examined
three of those four are in categories the current evidence cannot even classify, so consuming a reserve slot for them converts an unexplained failure into a spent slot and learns nothing
investigation consumes no reserve; it is the only move available with zero cost against the 40

the robots-bootstrap asymmetry means an unknown share of failures is attributable to single-sample network conditions on a one-shot request, and whether that share is large or negligible is exactly what the current evidence cannot say

p5Assessment.how: pure, incremental and monotonic - evaluated after every completed organisation, lowRawYieldCount counts over a list that only grows, so a PAUSE can never be un-triggered by a later high-yield run
p5Assessment.whyNot: P5's input is rawPageEvidenceCount - one integer per organisation - and carries no cause; a robots-redirect policy limit, a DNS failure, a TLS failure and an HTTP 500 all present to the gate as the same number, 0
p5Assessment.argumentForKeepingIt: it has fired three times and been right three times - twice exposing a genuine repairable capability limit (Option B, Option C-lite) and once, now, stopping a draw whose failure causes are not yet classifiable; a gate that keeps stopping a process that keeps having real problems is a gate that is working

governanceImpact.precedentNote: prior acquisition-policy changes v1->v2->v3 did NOT require methodology re-freeze because sampling and budgets stayed frozen, but DID require policy versioning and acquisition-plan amendments. This was analysed per option rather than assumed to transfer.

D.transitionLedgerUpdate: D1 census only; D2 entry for index 3

governanceImpact.whyMethodologyR3IsUntouchedInEveryOption: no option changes the frame, the draw, the split assignment, the 110/40 sizes, MIN_RAW_PAGE_EVIDENCE_PER_ORGANISATION, the P5 threshold, or any of the twelve frozen budget constants; a retry consumes the EXISTING MAX_TOTAL_REQUESTS_PER_ROOT = 60 rather than raising it
governanceImpact.whyBDAndEBumpThePolicyVersionButCDoesNot: the v1->v2->v3 precedent bumped because the REQUEST BOUNDARY moved - new requests became possible. B, D and E each make a request possible that was not possible before. C adds a column and changes no request whatsoever, so a bump would be a version number with no behavioural referent.
governanceImpact.firewallScopeNote: per the resolved phase-isolation decision, a change under src/orgunits/ is pinned by BASE..PHASE_TERMINAL ranges and the correct move is a NEW repair-scope test, never widening an existing firewall assertion. C must additionally be written so that phase2b.firewall.test.ts's existing no-raw-body assertions hold unchanged - error_subtype is a bounded enum, not a free-text or body column.
governanceImpact.censusStillRequiredEvenWhenTheAffectedSe: a census concluding 'zero affected' is itself the evidence that no slot needs revalidating; skipping it would leave that conclusion unrecorded

recommendedDecisionClass.name: TRANSPORT_OBSERVABILITY_MUST_BE_FIXED_BEFORE_RETRY_POLICY
reasoning: a bounded retry CAN technically be defined today for CONNECT_TIMEOUT, READ_TIMEOUT, CONNECTION_RESET and CONNECTION_REFUSED, because those categories are the persisted error_kind itself - so the literal claim in class B is true

but not one of the four current failures falls in those classes, and the classes that DO cover them (TLS_FAILURE, DNS_FAILURE) are exactly the two that cannot be safely subdivided with today's durable evidence
adopting B now would be adopting a rule that is correct and inert, and would make the pipeline APPEAR to have addressed transport resilience while leaving every observed failure unclassifiable

classes D1 and D2 are definable from http_status alone and are genuinely unblocked, but they address one index and D2's semantic footing is the weakest of anything considered - not a sufficient basis for the next decision
the binding constraint is therefore observability, and it should be fixed first
recommendedDecisionClass.whatCIsNot: not a claim that retrying is the right answer; it is the claim that the repository currently cannot TELL whether retrying is the right answer, that this is cheap to fix prospectively and impossible to fix retrospectively, and that every further acquisition run performed before the subtype column exists produces evidence with the same blind spot

ownDurability.ownCommitShaDeliberatelyAbsent: a record cannot truthfully contain the SHA of the commit that introduces it; this record's own commit is reported in the task's final report instead
